title: Why is Google cutting off Search from AI-free schools? Here are some theories
lede: NPR reports Google will withdraw Search entirely from schools that switch off AI Overviews, and weighs why, including a theory tied to Google's recent antitrust wins.

points: Schools that want AI Overviews off for students lose Google Search altogether, even as Los Angeles, Seattle and New York City districts ban classroom AI.
Former Googler Tracy Pizzo suggests a schools-only off switch would show Search and AI can be separated, undercutting a court finding that they are one product.
Antitrust experts NPR asked neither fully accepted nor dismissed that theory; Google pointed only to its announcement.
Common Sense Media rated AI Overviews an unacceptable risk, citing unsafe content and false information.
A long-time partner superintendent says the AI-or-nothing stance may have damaged Google's trust in education.

points.text: The top comment reframes it: Google is not cutting schools off but declining to build an AI-free version of Search.
Commenters compare Google's one-product defence to Microsoft's failed argument for bundling Internet Explorer.
Many suggest workarounds, such as appending udm=14 to queries or moving districts to DuckDuckGo's no-AI search.
Others see schools as a lock-in play, where early AI habits follow students into later digital use.
